data.description:
## Problem

`rebar fsck` reports **99 issues** in the tickets store, spanning 4 distinct classes. Two of
them compromise the identity model that the claim and close gates depend on.

## Evidence

Run `rebar fsck` from a current worktree. Current output ends:

```
fsck complete: 99 issues found
```

### 1. UNSIGNED_ENV — the active writer has no usable identity

```
UNSIGNED_ENV: 492a5c71-6cda-48a6-8134-02ff6a672739 — 0 of 104 event(s) signed, yet this env
wrote after authorship signing was adopted in this store.
```

`492a5c71-…` is the environment this session has been writing from. **Zero** of its 104 events
carry an authorship signature, so every ticket event it wrote is unattributable. Store-wide the
split is `56852 signed, 17993 unsigned`.

### 2. ENV_ID_MISMATCH — the same authors write under 3 environment ids

```
ENV_ID_MISMATCH: this environment ('492a5c71-…') has also written events under 2 other
environment id(s) (ade0f2ef-…, b8a354e0-…) — the same author(s) appear under both.
```

fsck names the cause directly: a tracker re-clone that did not carry over its git-ignored local
state (`.env-id`, `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`). The consequence is
stated just as directly — op-cert attestations signed by those identities **cannot be verified
here** and fail as `foreign_key` at the claim and close gates, so they must be re-earned.

### 3. FOREIGN_STORE_PATH — uncommitted strays in the tracker

```
FOREIGN_STORE_PATH: the tickets tracker holds 2 top-level path(s) that are not ticket data:
1022-d72f-4b89-49a3, af41-7784-737d-43e1. None are committed — they are working-tree strays.
```

These also surface as warnings on every plan-review run:
`skipping ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event … (debris of an interrupted write)`.

### 4. ORPHAN_EVENT / SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT — the bulk of the count

Two shapes. `ORPHAN_EVENT: <ticket>/<uuid>-{STATUS,EDIT,COMMENT,LINK,SIGNATURE,FILE_IMPACT}.json
— pre-snapshot event not captured in source_event_uuids`, and `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT:
… source UUID <u> still exists as <file>` (observed on `e082-0ad2-db98-4776` and
`eaba-0859-05f2-49e5`). Both describe snapshotting that did not correctly account for the
events it subsumed.

## Why this matters

The gates are the project's enforcement mechanism, and their trust root is the signature on an
operation certificate. An environment that signs nothing, and a store where one author appears
under 3 environment ids, together mean a gate cannot distinguish "this op was certified here"
from "this op carries a signature from an identity this clone cannot verify". That is the exact
condition `verify.require_environment` would enforce against — so this damage must be cleared
**before** the deferred op-cert environment binding described in ADR 0104 decision 3 and
`infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md` can be switched on. Flipping it against the
store in its current state would fail closed against legitimate work.

This is pre-existing damage, not something a single session introduced; it is filed because it
has been observed repeatedly and never recorded.

## Investigation notes

`rebar tracker-maintenance` offers only `--status`, `--clean`, and `--force` — there is **no**
fetch/sync verb, so the remedy for the identity classes is not obvious from the CLI surface and
needs to be determined as part of this work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause of `UNSIGNED_ENV` for `492a5c71-…` is established: determine why its writer produced 104 unsigned events, and whether `identity.signing_key` was unset, unreadable, or silently skipped. Record the evidence.
- [ ] The root cause of the 3-way `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` is established, including which clone(s) lost `.env-id`/`.opcert-key` and when.
- [ ] A documented remedy exists for re-establishing a clone's identity after a re-clone loses its git-ignored local state, reachable from the CLI without raw git in the tracker.
- [ ] The 2 `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH` strays are removed through a supported path, and plan-review stops emitting the `debris of an interrupted write` warnings.
- [ ] The `ORPHAN_EVENT`/`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` classes are either repaired or explained as benign with reasoning recorded.
- [ ] `rebar fsck` reports 0 issues, or every remaining issue is individually justified in a comment.
- [ ] A regression check prevents a clone from writing unsigned events silently — writing without a usable identity should be loud, not silent.
data.title: Tickets store fails fsck with 99 issues, including an active environment that signs nothing
